contribution: Ferdinand II of Aragon and Isabella I of Castile unified Spain through marriage in 1469, establishing the Spanish Empire. Their joint reign oversaw the completion of the Reconquista in 1492, expulsion of Jews and Muslims, funding of Columbus' voyages, and the beginning of Spanish colonization in the Americas. This created the foundation for Spain's golden age and global empire.
historical_significance: Spanish unification created the foundation for the first global empire, spreading Spanish language, culture, and Catholicism across the Americas and influencing world history.
thinker_traits: religious zeal, political pragmatism, visionary exploration, administrative innovation, military conquest, cultural synthesis
decision_points: marriage to Isabella, funding Columbus, Alhambra decree, conquest of Granada
philosophical_insights: unity through faith, marriage as political tool, exploration as national destiny, cultural assimilation through religion
critique: oppressive to non-Christians, exploitation of indigenous peoples, gold and silver depletion
legacy_impact: Spanish language spread across Americas, Catholic Church dominance in New World, global trade networks established, European colonization paradigm
